newsitem.title: UK: NWE straight-run fuel depressed in thin market.
newsitem.headline: NWE straight-run fuel depressed in thin market.

text.p: Low sulphur straight run fuel prices were depressed on Friday, weighed down by crude's weakness and lack of demand.
Offers were heard around the $101 fob level in northern Europe, with no trade seen done.
Sellers suggested refineries were switching attention back to crude to profit from its fall, and said buyers preferred to negotiate nearer mid-April, when straight-run cargoes fall due.
Two small packets of low sulphur were heard traded on Thursday from non-continental Europe. One was done confidentially, the other was believed heading to Scandinavia at around $108-$109 cif.
Low sulphur was just as unhappy in the Mediterranean, where one Russian cargo was believed looking for a home and attracting low bids. It was heard offered at a measly mean quotes minus a premium.
High sulphur Russian material was better supported and continues to appear at the Black Sea and Baltic ports intermittently. E-4 premiums were talked from $2 to $5, depending on quality.
One Russian E-4 was offered ex Klaipeda, with between one and 1.5 percent water, at three means plus $3.25.
